presets.name: 🏛️ TCJA Full Extension (CBO: $4.6T)
presets.description: Extend all TCJA individual provisions beyond 2025 sunset. Includes rate cuts, doubled standard deduction, SALT cap, pass-through deduction, CTC expansion.

status.label: Superseded by later law
status.note: Individual TCJA provisions were extended by the July 2025 reconciliation law (H.R. 1, P.L. 119-21). This preset reconstructs the pre-enactment official score of extension as then proposed.

current_law.reason: P.L. 119-21 made the individual TCJA provisions permanent (JCX-35-25 chapter 1, items 1-7), so they are in the baseline already. Current law is more generous than this preset on two pieces: the child tax credit is $2,200 and indexed, and the SALT cap is $40,000 through 2029 before returning to $10,000. The preset's tighter versions would raise revenue against current law; that is not scored here.

presets.name: 🏛️ TCJA Extension (No SALT Cap)
presets.description: Extend TCJA but repeal the \$10K SALT cap (adds ~\$1.9T to cost). Popular bipartisan proposal.

status.label: Superseded by later law
status.note: Individual TCJA provisions were extended by the July 2025 reconciliation law (H.R. 1, P.L. 119-21). This preset reconstructs the pre-enactment official score of extension as then proposed. The July 2025 law also modified the SALT cap, so the no-cap variant modeled here differs from what was enacted.

current_law.reason: TCJA is already permanent, so on current law this proposal is a repeal of the SALT cap. That is the Repeal SALT Cap preset, which is scored against the current-law cap path: $40,000 rising 1% a year through 2029, then $10,000 (P.L. 119-21 sec. 70120). The figure is that preset's score.
current_law.source: This model, on CBO's February 2026 baseline

presets.name: 🏛️ TCJA Rates Only
presets.description: Extend only the individual rate bracket cuts, not other TCJA provisions. CRS R48286 Table 1, "Reduced Individual Tax Rates": \$2,159B over FY2025-2034.

status.label: Superseded by later law
status.note: Individual TCJA provisions were extended by the July 2025 reconciliation law (H.R. 1, P.L. 119-21). This preset reconstructs the pre-enactment official score of extension as then proposed.

current_law.reason: P.L. 119-21 made the TCJA rate schedule permanent (JCX-35-25 chapter 1, item 1).

presets.name: 🏢 Biden Corporate 28% (Treasury: -$1.35T)
presets.description: Raise corporate rate from 21% to 28%. Treasury estimate (FY2025 Green Book): raises ~\$1.35T over 10 years.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: FY2025 Treasury Green Book proposal (Biden administration); not enacted.

presets.name: 🏢 Trump Corporate 15%
presets.description: Lower corporate rate from 21% to 15%, with bonus depreciation extended. Published estimates of the rate change alone run \$595B (PWBM) to \$673B (Tax Foundation) over ten years.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: 2024 campaign proposal; not enacted — the corporate rate remains 21%.

presets.name: 👶 Biden CTC Expansion (JCT: $1.6T)
presets.description: Expand CTC to \$3,600/\$3,000 per child, fully refundable. Based on 2021 ARP expansion.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: Proposal to make the temporary 2021 ARP expansion permanent; not enacted.

presets.name: 👶 CTC Extension (CBO: $600B)
presets.description: Extend current \$2,000 CTC beyond 2025 sunset. Without extension, reverts to \$1,000.

status.label: Superseded by later law
status.note: Individual TCJA provisions were extended by the July 2025 reconciliation law (H.R. 1, P.L. 119-21). This preset reconstructs the pre-enactment official score of extension as then proposed.

current_law.reason: P.L. 119-21 made the child tax credit permanent at $2,200, indexed (JCX-35-25 chapter 1, item 4). That is more generous than the $2,000 this preset extends; cutting back to $2,000 would raise revenue, which is not scored here.

presets.name: 💼 EITC Childless Expansion (Treasury: $163B)
presets.description: Triple EITC for childless workers (~\$1,500 max), expand age range to 19-65+.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: Proposal to make the temporary 2021 ARP expansion permanent; not enacted.

presets.name: 🏠 Estate Tax: Extend TCJA (CBO: $167B)
presets.description: Keep ~\$14M exemption (vs \$6.4M if TCJA expires). Costs ~\$167B over 10 years.

status.label: Superseded by later law
status.note: Individual TCJA provisions were extended by the July 2025 reconciliation law (H.R. 1, P.L. 119-21). This preset reconstructs the pre-enactment official score of extension as then proposed.

current_law.reason: P.L. 119-21 set the estate and gift exemption at $15 million from 2026, indexed (JCX-35-25 chapter 1, item 6). That is more generous than the TCJA exemption this preset extends; going back to the preset's level would raise revenue, which is not scored here.

presets.name: 🏠 Biden Estate Reform (-$450B)
presets.description: Lower exemption to \$3.5M, raise rate to 45%. Raises ~\$450B over 10 years.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: FY2025 Treasury Green Book proposal (Biden administration); not enacted.

presets.name: 🏠 Eliminate Estate Tax ($407B)
presets.description: Repeal the federal estate tax. Published estimate: about \$407B over CY2027-2036 (Tax Foundation, Options 3.0, Option 83), which repeals the gift tax too, so it is the broader of the two.

presets.name: 💰 SS Cap to 90% (CBO: -$800B)
presets.description: Raise Social Security cap to cover 90% of wages (~\$305K). Raises ~\$800B.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: Social Security solvency option from SSA/CBO options analyses; not enacted.

presets.name: 💰 SS Donut Hole $250K (-$1.43T)
presets.description: Apply the Social Security payroll tax to wages above \$250K (a donut hole). Published estimate: \$1,427B over FY2025-2034 (CBO, Options for Reducing the Deficit: 2025 to 2034, Option 62 alternative 2). This calculator's estimate is much larger because of how it sets the taxed wage band, a known miss.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: Social Security solvency option from SSA/CBO options analyses; not enacted.

presets.name: 💰 Eliminate SS Cap (-$3.2T)
presets.description: Eliminate Social Security wage cap entirely. Raises ~\$3.2T over 10 years.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: Social Security solvency option from SSA/CBO options analyses; not enacted.

presets.name: 💰 Expand NIIT (JCT: -$250B)
presets.description: Apply 3.8% NIIT to S-corp/partnership income. Raises ~\$250B over 10 years.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: FY2025 Treasury Green Book proposal (Biden administration); not enacted.

presets.name: ⚖️ AMT: Extend TCJA Relief ($1.36T)
presets.description: Extend TCJA's higher AMT exemptions (\$88K single, \$137K married filing jointly) past 2025. Published estimate: about \$1.36T over ten years (CRS R48286 Table 1, transcribing CBO).

status.label: Superseded by later law
status.note: Individual TCJA provisions were extended by the July 2025 reconciliation law (H.R. 1, P.L. 119-21). This preset reconstructs the pre-enactment official score of extension as then proposed.

current_law.reason: P.L. 119-21 made the higher AMT exemptions permanent, with new phase-out thresholds (JCX-35-25 chapter 1, item 7).

presets.name: ⚖️ Repeal Individual AMT ($450B)
presets.description: Fully repeal individual AMT. After TCJA expires, would cost ~\$450B over 10 years.

presets.name: ⚖️ Repeal Corporate AMT (+$220B)
presets.description: Repeal the 15% corporate book minimum tax (CAMT) enacted in the IRA in 2022. Published estimate: JCT scored enacting the CAMT as raising \$222.2B (JCX-18-22), so repeal costs about that much over ten years.

presets.name: 🏥 Extend ACA Enhanced PTCs ($335B)
presets.description: Extend enhanced premium tax credits (ARPA/IRA) past 2025. Costs ~\$335B over FY2025-2034 (CBO/JCT pub. 60437).

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: Extension proposal for the enhanced credits that were scheduled to lapse after 2025; not enacted.

presets.name: 🏥 Repeal ACA Premium Credits (-$1.1T)
presets.description: Repeal all ACA premium tax credits. Published estimate: saves about \$1.1T over ten years (CBO, 2024), with roughly 19 million people losing subsidized coverage.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: Legislative proposal; not enacted.

presets.name: 📋 Cap Employer Health Exclusion (-$450B)
presets.description: Cap tax exclusion for employer health insurance at \$50K. Raises ~\$450B over 10 years.

presets.name: 📋 Repeal SALT Cap ($1.17T)
presets.description: Remove the cap on the state and local tax deduction, scored against current law — P.L. 119-21 sec. 70120 sets it at \$40,400 in 2026 rising 1%/yr through 2029, phased down above \$500K of income, reverting to \$10K in 2030. Penn Wharton's ~\$1.17T prices the same repeal against a permanent \$10K cap, and ~\$197B against a baseline where the cap expires.

status.label: Partially overtaken by later law
status.note: The July 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21) raised the SALT cap to $40,000 in 2025, rising 1% a year through 2029 and reverting to $10,000 in 2030. This preset scores full repeal against that current-law path; the published figure in its label prices repeal of a permanent $10K cap.

presets.name: 📋 Eliminate Step-Up Basis (-$500B)
presets.description: Tax capital gains at death with \$1M exemption. Raises ~\$500B over 10 years.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: FY2025 Treasury Green Book proposal (Biden administration); not enacted.

presets.name: 📋 Cap Charitable Deduction (-$200B)
presets.description: Limit charitable deduction value to 28% rate. Raises ~\$200B over 10 years.

presets.name: Top Rate to 39.6% (Biden FY2025)
presets.description: +2.6pp on income above \$400K, restoring the pre-TCJA 39.6% top rate. Treasury FY2025 Green Book estimate: raises ~\$252B over 10 years.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: FY2025 Treasury Green Book proposal (Biden administration); not enacted.

presets.name: Progressive Millionaire Tax
presets.description: A 5pp surtax on income above \$1M, scored on the AGI-inclusive base, with capital gains and qualified dividends included. No official score: nothing published scores this reform, so the figure shown is this calculator's own estimate. The AGI-inclusive base is a design choice, by analogy with the Warren and Medicare surtaxes, not something read from a source.

presets.name: Middle Class Tax Cut
presets.description: 2pp cut for households earning \$50K+

presets.name: Flat Tax Reform
presets.description: Lower all rates by 5pp (illustrative)

presets.name: Warren Ultra-Millionaire Surtax
presets.description: A 3pp surtax on AGI above \$2M, Warren-style, scored on the AGI-inclusive base, with realized capital gains and qualified dividends included.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: Senate proposal; not enacted.

presets.name: Top Rate to 45%
presets.description: Raise the top marginal rate from 37% to 45% on income above the 37% bracket floor (\$609,350 single, 2025). It sits at the upper end of progressive proposals. No official score exists for it, so the figure shown is this calculator's own estimate.

presets.name: High-Earner Medicare Surcharge 2pp
presets.description: A 2pp Medicare surcharge on wage and investment income above \$400K, scored on the AGI-inclusive base Treasury's FY2025 Green Book row uses. It extends the logic of the NIIT's 3.8% surtax to a broader base, and is similar in structure to the Biden 2025 Medicare surtax proposal.

presets.name: 🌍 Biden GILTI Reform (-$374B)
presets.description: Country-by-country GILTI at 21% and no QBAI exemption. Published estimate: raises about \$374B over ten years (Treasury, FY2025 Green Book).

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: FY2025 Treasury Green Book proposal (Biden administration); not enacted.

presets.name: 🌍 Repeal FDII (-$158B)
presets.description: Repeal the deduction for foreign-derived intangible income (FDII). Published estimate: raises about \$158B over ten years (Treasury, FY2025 Green Book, before the R&D proposal Treasury pairs it with).

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: FY2025 Treasury Green Book proposal (Biden administration); not enacted.

presets.name: 🌍 Pillar Two Adoption (-$80B)
presets.description: Adopt the OECD Pillar Two 15% global minimum tax. Published estimate: raises about \$80B (JCT).

presets.name: 🌍 Biden International Package (-$632B)
presets.description: The full Biden international package: per-country GILTI at 21%, FDII repeal and the UTPR. Published estimate: raises about \$632B over ten years (Treasury, FY2025 Green Book subtotal).

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: FY2025 Treasury Green Book proposal (Biden administration); not enacted.

presets.name: 🔍 IRA Enforcement Funding (-$180B)
presets.description: IRA IRS enforcement funding. CBO: raises ~\$180B of revenue over FY2022-2031 (pub. 58390), about \$101B net of the \$79B appropriation.

status.label: Enacted
status.note: Enacted in the Inflation Reduction Act (2022); later laws rescinded part of the funding. This preset reconstructs CBO's 2022 score of the provision as enacted, so it is not new revenue on top of current law.

presets.name: 🔍 Double IRS Enforcement (-$340B)
presets.description: Double IRS enforcement funding beyond IRA levels (about \$16B a year). Published estimate: about \$340B over ten years (Treasury and Sarin-Summers, 2021), with diminishing returns. Illustrative: an unfitted reconstruction a long way from that figure, shown for the shape of the policy rather than as an estimate of it.

presets.name: 🔍 High-Income Enforcement
presets.description: Targeted enforcement on returns above \$400K and large partnerships, at \$5B a year. No official score: nothing published scores a targeted increase. CBO scores untargeted funding only, \$20B of funding for -\$41B of deficit and \$40B for -\$63B (publication 59972, FY2024-2034). The figure shown is this calculator's own estimate.

presets.name: 💊 Expand Drug Negotiation (-$500B)
presets.description: Negotiate prices for 50 Medicare drugs (against the IRA's 20) and remove exclusivity delays. No published score of this design exists. Illustrative: an unfitted reconstruction, shown for the shape of the policy rather than as an estimate of it.

presets.name: 💊 Universal Insulin Cap ($11B)
presets.description: A \$35 a month insulin cap for Medicare and private insurance. A cost-sharing cap shifts costs onto plans, so CBO scores it as adding about \$11B to the deficit over ten years. Illustrative: an unfitted reconstruction a long way from that published figure, shown for the shape of the policy rather than as an estimate of it.

presets.name: 💊 International Reference Pricing (-$100B)
presets.description: Cap Medicare drug prices at 120% of the OECD average. No published budget score of this design exists; the figure it used to be compared with came from a price index, not a cost estimate. Illustrative: an unfitted reconstruction, shown for the shape of the policy rather than as an estimate of it.

presets.name: 💊 Comprehensive Drug Reform
presets.description: Expanded negotiation, a universal insulin cap and manufacturer discounts together. No official score: nothing published scores the three combined, and the nearest published figures are much smaller components (CBO put the IRA's own negotiation at \$98.5B over FY2022-2031). The figure shown is this calculator's own estimate. Illustrative: shown for the shape of the policy rather than as an estimate of it.

presets.name: 🏭 Trump Universal 10% Tariff (-$2.17T)
presets.description: A 10% tariff on all imports. Published estimate: raises about \$2.17T over ten years, conventional (Tax Foundation, FF861).

status.label: Partially overtaken by later law
status.note: Broad tariff actions were imposed by executive order in 2025; this preset models a stylized schedule, not the enacted structure.

presets.name: 🏭 Trump 60% China Tariff (-$650B)
presets.description: 60% tariff on all Chinese imports (~\$430B base). CRFB's *Options to Raise Tariff Revenue* scores it at \$650B over FY2026-2035, and notes savings would run about 15% lower on FY2025-2034.

status.label: Partially overtaken by later law
status.note: China-focused tariff actions were imposed by executive order in 2025; this preset models a stylized schedule, not the enacted structure.

presets.name: 🏭 25% Auto Tariff (-$386B)
presets.description: A 25% tariff on imported vehicles and parts (about \$380B of imports). Published estimate: raises about \$386B over ten years, conventional (Tax Foundation tariff tracker).

presets.name: 🏭 25% Steel/Aluminum Tariff (-$60B)
presets.description: 25% tariff on steel and aluminum imports (~\$50B base).

presets.name: 🏭 Reciprocal Tariffs (-$1.5T)
presets.description: Match trading partners' tariff rates (~20pp average increase). Published conventional estimates of the announced schedule span \$1.4-1.8T; the official score shown anchors on Tax Foundation's \$1.5T.
presets.cbo_source: CRFB / Tax Foundation / Yale Budget Lab

status.label: Partially overtaken by later law
status.note: Reciprocal-tariff actions were imposed by executive order in 2025; this preset models a stylized schedule, not the enacted structure.

presets.name: 🌱 Repeal IRA Clean Energy Credits (-$851B)
presets.description: Full repeal of the IRA clean energy tax credits. Published estimate: about \$851B over FY2025-2034 (Tax Foundation, McBride, House Oversight testimony, May 2025).

status.label: Partially overtaken by later law
status.note: The July 2025 reconciliation law curtailed several IRA clean-energy credits. This preset models full repeal as scored before that law.

current_law.reason: P.L. 119-21 already ended or cut back many of these credits. JCT puts those terminations at $542.7 billion of revenue over FY2025-2034 (JCX-35-25 chapter 5, subchapter A). Repealing what is left would save less than the full-repeal figure, but this model has not scored the remainder. Subtracting JCT's number from Tax Foundation's would mix two estimators, so it is not done here.

presets.name: 🌱 Carbon Tax \$50/ton (-$1.7T)
presets.description: A \$50 per ton CO2 tax rising 5% a year. No published score of this design exists. The \$1.7T on the Build list is a CBO-style estimate, not a CBO or JCT figure, and the figure shown here is this calculator's own estimate.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: Analytic option scored by CBO; never enacted.

presets.name: 🌱 Carbon Tax \$25/ton
presets.description: A \$25 per ton CO2 tax rising 5% a year. No official score of this design covers this window. CBO and JCT's Options for Reducing the Deficit: 2023 to 2032 scores a \$25 per tonne tax rising 5% plus inflation at -\$865B over FY2023-2032, a different decade, so the figure shown is this calculator's own estimate.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: Analytic option scored by CBO; never enacted.

presets.name: 🌱 Repeal EV Credits (-$182B)
presets.description: Repeal the \$7,500 clean-vehicle credit (sec. 30D) and the commercial clean-vehicle credit (sec. 45W). Published estimate: JCT put ending these credits at about \$182B over FY2025-2034 (JCX-35-25), in its score of P.L. 119-21.

status.label: Superseded by later law
status.note: The July 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21) ended the clean-vehicle credits (secs. 30D and 45W) for vehicles acquired after 30 September 2025; JCT's estimate of that law (JCX-35-25) is the published figure in this preset's label. This preset scores repeal against pre-2025 law, where the credits continue.

current_law.reason: P.L. 119-21 ended the clean-vehicle credits (secs. 30D and 45W) for vehicles acquired after 30 September 2025 (JCX-35-25 chapter 5, items A.2 and A.3). There is nothing left to repeal.

presets.name: 🌱 Extend IRA Credits Beyond 2032
presets.description: Extend the IRA clean energy credits five years beyond the 2032 sunset. No official score: published figures cover the credits as enacted or their repeal, never a five-year extension. The figure shown is this calculator's own estimate.

status.label: Proposed — not enacted
status.note: Extension proposal; not enacted.
